answer: One workable design: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because prism only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. In practice wander is enforced by the ledger itself: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any zephyr approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
